name: Mannequin Pussy
label: Epitaph
lede: A Connecticut duo with a drum kit and a tape deck became Philadelphia's loudest love song, and in 2024 Pitchfork gave them an 8.8.

eras.title: Two kids, a drum kit and a tape deck
eras.text: Marisa Dabice and Athanasios Paul start a two-piece in Connecticut, put out EPs with names like Bonerjamz!, and learn the DIY circuit on cassettes and split tours. By 2013 Dabice is in Philadelphia, where the band finds its room.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mannequin Pussy · Crack Magazine · Philadelphia Inquirer
years.h: [[Mannequin Pussy|e160f589-dbe6-4b8f-88b5-f528ff4443b4]] starts as a two-piece: Dabice and Paul
years.p: Marisa "Missy" Dabice sang and played guitar; Athanasios Paul, a friend from school, played drums. Crack puts the start in Connecticut.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the band to October 2010 and says Dabice and Paul met in school. Crack Magazine places the early band in Connecticut, before the move to Philadelphia.

The Inquirer says the band as it is known today took shape in 2013, shortly before Dabice relocated to Philadelphia, which is why some profiles give 2013 as the start.

years.h: Two EPs: Bonerjamz! and Meatslave
years.p: The band's first releases, both 2011, from a duo still working out what it was. The titles tell you the mood.

years.h: A split cassette with Idaho's Art Fad: 13 songs
years.p: Banditos on Trash Palace Tapes, a tour tape shared with Art Fad. "Clue Juice" also landed on the Leisure Rules comp from Reeks Of Effort the same month.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists both July 2012 tape releases: the Art Fad split, with thirteen Mannequin Pussy songs on it, and the Reeks Of Effort cassette compilation that carried "Clue Juice".

years.h: Drew Adler takes the drum stool; Paul moves to guitar
years.p: The duo becomes a proper band: Drew Adler on drums, Athanasios Paul on guitar, Dabice out front.

years.h: The Rotunda pays $100, the most they had ever made
years.p: Dabice had moved to Philadelphia after meeting players like Nicole Snyder and Rachel Gagliardi of [[Slutever|f8887032-74fc-4ce0-87df-963ab10b2629]] on tour, and a West Philly room gave the band its first real night's pay.
years.xp: The Philadelphia Inquirer says Dabice relocated from Connecticut after meeting women musicians including Nicole Snyder and Rachel Gagliardi of Slutever while touring. It describes a 2013 show at the Rotunda in West Philadelphia that paid the band $100, "the most money we had ever made."

years.h: Gypsy Pervert arrives as a cassette-only first album
years.p: Out in a limited run on Rarebit Records, a little over eighteen minutes of noise, melody and shouting.

eras.title: Gypsy Pervert becomes Mannequin Pussy
eras.text: A record deal, a rename and a new rhythm section. By the end of 2016 the band has the lineup and the songs that get it noticed outside Philadelphia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mannequin Pussy (album) · Wikipedia: Mannequin Pussy
years.h: Tiny Engines reissues the debut under a new title
years.p: Gypsy Pervert became Mannequin Pussy after the band worried the original title read as a slur against Romani people.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the album was retitled when the band signed to Tiny Engines in 2014, because of concerns about the original title's pejorative connotations toward Romani people. The September 9, 2014 release was a co-release between Rarebit Records and Tiny Engines; the band produced it with D. A. Stern.

Frank Valish of Under the Radar wrote that the songs "hit you over the head like an anvil" while holding girl-group melodies and shoegaze haze.

years.h: Kaleen Reading replaces Adler on drums
years.p: [[Kaleen Reading|2c1636c7-37e0-459c-a64e-3d28f0343d32]] takes the kit and stays: she is still the band's drummer a decade later.

years.h: Colins "Bear" Regisford joins on bass and vocals
years.p: Bear Regisford makes it a four-piece with Dabice, Paul and Reading, and adds a second voice the band leans on from then on.

years.h: Romantic: seventeen minutes, recorded by the band
years.p: Tracked at Big Mamas Recording in Philadelphia and mixed by the band itself, it is the record where hardcore speed and pop hooks start to share a song.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave Romantic 7.6 and The A.V. Club an A-minus, per Wikipedia. Rolling Stone ranked the title track No. 14 on its 50 best songs of 2016, and Stereogum made the album its album of the week.

Dabice has said the songs came from two years of working through depression and anxiety and finding out she was not alone in it.

eras.title: Patience pays off
eras.text: Touring, a sharper video language and a move to Epitaph. By 2019 the band has its breakout record, a Best-of-year placement at Pitchfork and a song that every year-end list wants.

years.h: Audiotree Live catches the four-piece on tape
years.p: A live EP on Audiotree, a record of a touring band that had outgrown the basement.

years.h: "Pledge" video: a woman controlled, then free
years.p: Dabice told DIY the clip follows a woman whose movements are dictated by a man and the people around her, until she makes a declaration to herself.
years.xp: The video went up on YouTube on May 30, 2017. Dabice's description to DIY magazine was of a woman whose movements are controlled by a man and by those around her, and of the declaration she is able to make once she frees herself.

years.src: Wikipedia: Patience (Mannequin Pussy album) · Wikipedia: Mannequin Pussy · The Ringer
years.h: Patience: Will Yip, Studio 4 and an 8.4 from Pitchfork
years.p: Recorded in Conshohocken with [[Will Yip|282e2957-fd09-4260-babf-50f1d57eeb75]] and released June 21 on Epitaph, it ran 25 minutes and put the band on Pitchfork's best-of-2019 list at No. 35.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Quinn Moreland gave Patience 8.4 and called it one of the best punk rock records of 2019, per Wikipedia. "Drunk II" was No. 16 on Pitchfork's 100 best songs of 2019. In 2026, Rolling Stone ranked the album No. 42 on its 100 greatest punk albums.

Dabice's own summary of the theme was un-learning self-hatred and being patient with yourself and others. Wikipedia dates the Epitaph signing to 2019; The Ringer puts it in 2016 (see questions).

years.h: "Cream" gets a 1970s horror video
years.p: Director Hanna Hamilton took cues from 1970s horror for the clip, released days before Patience.

years.h: Tiny Engines goes on hiatus over unpaid royalties
years.p: Wikipedia reports the old label paused amid accounting disputes over unpaid artist royalties, which affected Mannequin Pussy.
years.xp: Tiny Engines had released the band's 2014 and 2016 albums. The band later bought back its masters (see 2022-23) and started its own imprint.

eras.title: Stolen vans, a Mare of Easttown and a fourth person on guitar
eras.text: A pandemic cancels a tour, a van gets stolen twice and the band's songs land in an HBO murder mystery. The original guitarist steps away and the core four become three.

years.h: Pandemic cancels the Best Coast tour
years.p: The band's touring income vanished, and Dabice later said they lost their main form of income and missed some of their biggest opportunities.
years.xp: Crack reports the March 2020 Best Coast tour was halted by the pandemic, and that the van was broken into in Philadelphia, its catalytic converter taken, then stolen outright and found abandoned across town three days later. Dabice told Guitar.com the band "lost our main form of income" in lockdown.

years.h: Athanasios Paul leaves after eleven years
years.p: The founding guitarist departed "to begin a new chapter in his life," leaving [[Marisa Dabice|7826f103-696c-43eb-8786-cbc38300b471]], Reading and Regisford as a three-piece.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives March 18, 2021 for the announcement. Crack says Paul left in early 2020, so the date conflicts (see questions).

years.h: Dabice plays an FBI agent in Japanese Breakfast's "Be Sweet"
years.p: A cameo in [[Japanese Breakfast|8c529495-91f5-4e2f-b71b-adcb66878d04]]'s video.

years.src: Wikipedia: Perfect (Mannequin Pussy EP) · Crack Magazine
years.h: Perfect EP: five songs cut in two days with Will Yip
years.p: Yip returned from Patience; it was the first time the band walked in without pre-written songs. Pitchfork's Arielle Gordon gave it 7.2.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the EP was recorded between August 2020 and February 2021. Crack reports it was tracked at Studio 4 in Conshohocken and that all five songs were finished in two days.

years.h: HBO's Mare of Easttown has a fake band play Mannequin Pussy songs
years.p: "Who You Are" and "In Love Again" were performed by the miniseries' fictional band Androgynous, and Dabice later said the placement gave the band "cultural and artistic legitimacy."
years.xp: The Philadelphia Inquirer credits Mare of Easttown (2021) with that legitimacy, in Dabice's words. The show is set in suburban Pennsylvania.

years.big: Even if they hate it, they're calling it perfect.
years.src: Crack Magazine · Wikipedia: Perfect (Mannequin Pussy EP)
years.h: What the title of Perfect was for
years.p: Dabice on why she named the EP Perfect, quoted in Crack.
years.xp: Crack Magazine quotes Dabice on the title as a reply to people who will pick the record apart. Wikipedia lists Pitchfork at 7.2, Clash at 8 and a Metacritic score of 80.

years.h: Van and trailer stolen in Akron, Ohio, $50,000 of gear gone
years.p: The Ford Econoline and trailer were taken during the tour; the band finished the remaining dates on borrowed gear.
years.xp: Wikipedia puts the theft on October 30, 2021 and values the equipment at more than $50,000. The same month the band added [[Carolyn Haynes|5a7b8fb2-ce81-43c1-90f8-b1257f45af63]] (guitar, keyboards) and [[Maxine Steen|74a4fb47-9fde-49ea-8c6d-3523b1254b0d]] (guitar) as touring members.

eras.title: Their own label, their best record
eras.text: The band owns its back catalogue, starts Romantic Records and records its fourth album in Los Angeles with John Congleton. Pitchfork puts it at No. 11 of the year.

years.h: The band buys its masters back from Tiny Engines
years.p: It paid for the rights to Romantic, the record Tiny Engines had put out in 2016.
years.xp: Guitar.com dates the buyback to the year before its August 2023 announcement; Wikipedia places the buyback in August 2023 alongside the label launch (see questions).

years.h: Romantic Records launches with Romantic on vinyl
years.p: The band's own imprint opened with a limited reissue of its out-of-print 2016 album, and thanked Tiny Engines for being among its first supporters.

years.h: Maxine Steen becomes a full member
years.p: After two years on tour, [[Maxine Steen|74a4fb47-9fde-49ea-8c6d-3523b1254b0d]] goes from hired guitarist to fourth member, restoring the four-piece.

years.h: The title track lands, shot on a farm
years.p: "I Got Heaven" arrived August 28, 2023, nine months before the album, with a video by Mason Mercer and Anthony Miralles set on a farm.

years.src: Wikipedia: I Got Heaven · GRAMMY.com · The Ringer · Philadelphia Inquirer
years.h: I Got Heaven: Pitchfork 8.8, Best New Music, No. 11 of 2024
years.p: Released March 1 on Epitaph and produced by John Congleton in Los Angeles, it is the band's fourth album and its first made outside Philadelphia.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave the record 8.8 and Best New Music per Wikipedia's reception box, and later ranked it No. 11 on its list of the 50 best albums of 2024. Metacritic scored it 89. Exclaim! put it No. 6 and The Ringer named it the No. 2 album and Mannequin Pussy its band of 2024.

Congleton came through Epitaph founder Brett Gurewitz. Dabice told GRAMMY.com the songs grew out of two years off from dating after three members' breakups at once, and that "Split Me Open" came the day after a psychedelic trip at a family cabin in New Hampshire. The Ringer says Pitchfork later ranked it the 87th best album of the 2020s. "Loud Bark" opened the 2025 series The Hunting Wives, per Wikipedia.

years.h: KEXP session: the album live
years.p: The band played a full performance at KEXP in Seattle on the tour for I Got Heaven.

years.h: Cancelled second European leg, then a Best Friends Forever night
years.p: Dabice scrapped the second European run on a month's notice for her wellbeing, took almost two months to recover, and then played Best Friends Forever.
years.xp: The Ringer reports Dabice took nearly two months to recover, with therapy and fitness, and called the band at Best Friends Forever in October 2024 "the most exciting, modern group of rock stars that anyone got to see."
